items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: at that time there was a pianist called Arthur Matthews, who wrote "Worry Blues", who had a music school. I could have had lessons in harmony with him for 50 cents a lessons... Instead, I learned by hanging out with older musicians.

ctx.x: Edgar, myself and an amateur alto player named Alex Baker, used to rehearse at Edgar's house or Alex's house twice every week. I dont remember how I met Alex but I remember that he lived on Court Street. We could get orchestrations from a couple of music publishing stores up town and one we received was "Three O'clock In The Morning", which was a waltz. There was one place in this number where the trumpet part went as high as A above the staff and that was a note I could not reach, so I made a turn on the note…

My reading started to get better when a piano player named Clarence Trotter joined out little rehearsals. He would play the number while we looked over the parts. Then we'd play them slowly until we had a good idea how the notes sounded. Then we'd give the tempo a little lift, and then a little more until we had the number up to speed.
